*UPX, the new symbol of Akihabara, was located right in front of the station.*

*Viktor Chondria University.*

*Also, this convention was holding another seminar by Viktor Chondria University, after the one held this summer.*
*Of course, that interested me, too.*
*Summer...*
Rintaro: “...”
*An image of her as she was then flashed through my mind.*

*All of the questioners were skeptical of the professor’s theory, and many of them seemed to be outright challenging him.*
*I started to get upset.*
*This was Dr. Leskinen’s research, but it was also Kurisu’s.*
*I knew better than anyone that it worked, and the sight of so many people refusing to give it a chance infuriated me.*
*Were these people really scientists?*
*I tried to keep myself under control and looked back towards the podium.*
Maho: “...”
*...Was she mad?*
*She certainly looked disappointed.*
*Dr. Leskinen was very polite with the rude questioners, acknowledging the problems with the theory. She was very different.*
*Her anger was starting to seep into her interpreting, too.*
*I felt a kind of kinship with her.*

Questioner: “From a medical standpoint, this is just reckless. It’s absolutely impossible to rewrite digital data back into the brain. It’s insane.”
Questioner: “I read the essay in ‘Science’, and I have to say, I don’t believe it.”

*That was the one thing I couldn’t ignore.*

*I saw a flash of white teeth as our eyes met.*

*I’d thought I was calm, but I guess I let my emotions get away from me. I hadn’t grown up at all in the past six months.*
*If Kurisu was here, she’d make fun of me again...*
*I could feel the rest of the audience staring at me coldly. It hurt.*

*This was something unbelievable, wasn’t it?*
*It felt very different than a typical AI. I could tell that much.*
*It wasn’t answering the questions it was given?*
*And because they were embarrassing?*
*Was it programmed to respond like that to certain questions, for the purposes of this demonstration?*
*It was possible that’s all it was, but...*
*If that conversation wasn’t programmed in advance...*

*Maho walked back to the professor.*

Amadeus Maho: “I eventually forget about unnecessary information.”
Amadeus Maho: “Or rather, I become unable to access those memories, just like all of you.”
Amadeus Maho: “For example, the color of the pajamas I wore a week ago. There’s no reason I shouldn’t know this, but right now I can’t remember it.”
Amadeus Maho: “That’s because this information isn’t necessary to my survival. The same goes for all of you.”
Amadeus Maho: “So as you can see, Amadeus’s memory inputs and outputs are very similar to a human’s.”
Maho: “This result surprised us, too, and we’re currently researching it, but we still don’t know exactly how it works.”
*As Maho finished up, Dr. Leskinen took the microphone back. She resumed interpreting as he continued the lecture.*
Maho: “Another thing that surprised us is that Amadeus is capable of deliberate lies.”
Maho: “By ‘deliberate,’ I mean it lies of its own free will, not as the result of any programming error.”
Maho: “Lies are one method that humans use to communicate with one another.”
Maho: “And just like a human, Amadeus can use its memories to decide if lying would be best. If so, it will lie without hesitation.”
Maho: “Don’t tell them that, Professor.”
Maho: “I can’t lie without hesitation. I have a conscience, you know.”
Leskinen: “I’m so sorry. And...”
*Dr. Leskinen cut off.*
*He seemed to be hesitating.*
*Maho didn’t seem especially surprised by this. Maybe she knew the reason.*
*But the moment passed, and the professor continued.*
*And Maho translated his words like there was nothing shocking about them at all.*
Maho: “As we continue our research, we eventually believe that–”
Maho: “It may be possible to give Amadeus a soul, just like a living human’s.”
*I was stunned.*
*A soul...?*
*Should one of the leading brain scientists in the world really be using a word with such a vague definition?*
Maho: “This would mean the creation of artificial intelligence, in the true sense.”
*The whole hall got very quiet.*
*And it was sheer chaos for a while after that, as everyone tried to debate their own personal theories with Dr. Leskinen at once.*

Assailant: “...Woe to the world... Such things must come... woe to the person through whom they come...”

*And then he staggered to his feet.*

*The crowd began to scream.*

*The attacker had been shot?*
*Did he shoot himself?*
*No... that gunshot was clearly different than the last ones.*
Rintaro: “W-Who’s there?”
*Who had just fired?!*
*I looked around.*
*I could see several policemen coming from the entrance.*
*But none of them had their guns drawn.*
*And the crowd was nothing but security and hotel staff. I couldn’t see any of them carrying a gun.*
*So who had fired? And where had they fired from?*
*And the way they took the attacker’s head off with a single shot...*
*Not just anyone could do that.*
Rintaro: “What... is going on?”
*Of course, no one told me.*
*Afterward, the police took us into custody.*
*We were taken to the police station, and questioned until late into the night.*
*The sun was almost about to rise by the time we left.*
*The police took me home in a patrol car.*
*Dr. Leskinen and Maho were having the police take them back to their hotel in Wako, so we split up in front of the police station.*
*We never did find out why the man had attacked us.*

==========SG0_B01_07.scx.txt==========
*For the first time in almost four months, I felt like the whole world was twisting.*
*Who was it?*
*Who had changed the world line?!*
*I didn’t do anything. I hadn’t interfered with the world.*
*So why was the world doing this to me?!*
Rintaro: “...”
*I opened my eyes.*
*Things had already taken on different colors.*
*The world kept wavering, until once again it became fixed to a single point in time.*
*I wasn’t looking at a warm, cheerful party in the lab anymore.*
*I was outside.*
*It was raining.*
*The rain was falling on my face, in drops so large that it hurt.*
*It was a midwinter rain. It was freezing cold, and I could feel it sapping the strength from my body.*
*My view stopped twisting.*
*I was staring at the broad back of a man I didn’t know.*
*I could hear the sound of many boots stamping through the mud, mingling with falling rain.*
*The stench was terrible. The smell of sewage was so strong it hurt to breathe. And it was mixed with the awful smell of burning rubber and plastic.*
*Where was I? What was I doing right now?*
*Things around me had changed so much.*
*I tried to understand the situation I was in, but my brain was having an awful time keeping up.*
Man’s voice: “We’re almost there. Hang in there.”
*When I stopped, a rough hand patted me on the shoulder encouragingly.*
*I looked around to see a man my age, with a strong, powerful face.*
*It was a face I’d never seen. I didn’t know him... probably.*
*The man was wearing the camo outfit and equipment I’d often seen the Self-Defense Force wear on the news. He was carrying an assault rifle on his shoulder.*
*There were seven or eight people around me, all dressed the same.*
*They surrounded me in a circular formation and walked forward silently, as they kept a careful eye on the area around them.*
Rintaro: (Are these people... the Self-Defense Force?)
*And then I realized...*
*I was wearing the same camo uniform they were.*
Rintaro: (I’m in the SDF, too?!)
*I touched my bicep to check, but there was no muscle. It was flabby and weak. Unlike the others, I wasn’t carrying any weapons.*
*Then what was going on here?*
*It felt like these seven or eight tough-looking SDF guys were all guarding me...*
*Since when was I that important?*
*Still confused, I dragged myself onwards.*
*Where was I, anyway?*
*It was a long path filled with dark brown mud.*
*The walls formed a tall silhouette to the left and right.*
*The path was filled with garbage and concrete rubble, and sometimes we had to force our way past it.*
*I looked up past the high walls. Despite the rain, the moon in the night sky was strangely red and a little too bright.*
*It was thanks to the moon that we were able to walk down a path like this without flashlights.*
Rintaro: “Huh?”
*Sound. I heard a sound.*
*It was... the sound of water.*
*I looked over and saw a hole opened in one of the walls. Filthy water was pouring out. The water formed dozens of little rivers that blocked our path.*
*So that was it. This was the bottom of a river that had dried up. What looked like high walls were the river dikes.*
Rintaro: “Where are we?!”
*I turned towards the man who had spoken to me a bit ago, and yelled so that my voice could be heard over the rain.*
SDF personnel: “Ssh! Don’t make any loud noises.”
Rintaro: “Oh, sorry...”
SDF personnel: “We’re almost through the city center. If we can make it to Nerima Garrison, there’ll be a car waiting for you. So just keep walking–”
*But– his words cut off there.*
*Everyone seemed more tense than ever.*
*One of them grabbed me and pushed me toward the side of the riverbed.*
*Everyone put their backs against the wall and held their breath.*
*I could hear the sound of a helicopter’s rotors in the distance.*
*No, more than just one.*
*They were getting closer.*
*I had no idea what was going on, but I could feel my heart start to beat faster.*
SDF personnel: “Get in the shadow of that car.”
*Past several meters of rubble lay an overturned car.*
*It must’ve fallen into the riverbed after the water had disappeared. The entire body was bent inward, and the roof was completely crushed.*
*I lay down in the stinking mud and slid into the shadow of the overturned car.*
*At the same time, the SDF soldiers were issuing each other orders, as if this was something they’d planned for already.*
*Two of them stayed by my side, and everyone else ran back the way we’d come.*
*They all climbed up crevices and outcroppings on the wall, then disappeared over the edge of the dike and out of my view.*
*Shortly after...*
Rintaro: “...!”
*Those were... gunshots.*
*And not just a single shot from a handgun, or anything like that.*
*This was the sound of war.*
*I could hear the helicopters get further away, drawn by the gunfire.*
Rintaro: “...Oh no.”
*In this world line, was Japan... at war?*
*–The Third World War.*
*I remembered Suzuha’s words.*
*I happened to look inside the crushed car...*
Rintaro: “...!”
*I could see the corpses of a man, a woman, and a small child hanging upside down, still attached to their seat belts.*
*They were all covered in dried black blood. They looked like mannequins at a bad haunted house.*
Rintaro: “Aaah... Aaah...”
*And then I realized...*
*I’d been so focused on moving forward that I hadn’t noticed what they were, but I’d seen similar “mannequins” sunk into the mud...*
*I could see their arms, the bones and ragged muscle exposed to the air, reaching up to the sky as if seeking salvation.*
Rintaro: “Ugh...”
*I put my hand over my mouth to stifle a scream.*
*Those weren’t mannequins...!*
SDF personnel: “Now! Get along the side of the wall and move!”
Rintaro: “Huh...?”
SDF personnel: “We’re changing the route. Come on, stand up.”
*He pulled me up. My knees were shaking from shock and exhaustion.*
SDF personnel: “The others are drawing away the Soviet helicopters, but that won’t last long. Hurry.”
Rintaro: “The Soviet Union?”
*My mind was dulled from the terror, but it seemed like there was something off about what he just said.*
SDF personnel: “Get a hold of yourself. Do you know how many people have died to protect you?”
Rintaro: “Protect... me? Why?”
SDF personnel: “We haven’t been told why. But we were told to lay down our lives for you if we had to. And that you could change this country’s future.”
*A helicopter passed over the riverbed. The bright searchlight passed by for a moment, but thankfully, the shadow of the dike hid us.*
SDF personnel: “This way.”
*The young SDF soldier, whose name I didn’t even know, pulled me inside one of the holes in the concrete.*
*When I looked closely, I could see that it was the entrance to a sewer.*
*It was just big enough for a single person to pass through.*
*Struggling against the flow of water that came up to my knees, I pressed on through the darkness.*
*My sense of smell had already gone numb, so I didn’t have to worry about the stench of the sewage.*
*Once inside, we came to several branching paths.*
*The SDF soldiers seemed to know which one would lead where, and they marched on without hesitation.*
*And then we came out of the sewer and back into a riverbed.*
*It was dried up, just like the one we’d just been through.*
*I didn’t know if it was the same river, or another one, and the two soldiers didn’t tell me.*
*Either way, I was glad to be finally out of the foul-smelling darkness, and I tried to take a deep breath and fill my lungs with fresh air.*
*But-*
Rintaro: “Ugh... ah...?”
*Halfway through I realized that the riverbed smelled even worse than the sewer. I took an involuntary step back, and then another.*
*The sight in front of me was just that terrible.*
*What was once a riverbed was now filled with bodies.*
*Some of them had been burnt totally black, so it was impossible to tell how much death lay before me.*
*And in the distance, I could see what looked like bonfires.*
*They were burning despite the rain.*
*The fires were consuming the mountains of flesh that once were human bodies.*
SDF personnel: “We’re almost there. I know it’s rough, but can you run?”
Rintaro: “Huh? Uh... yeah.”
*The SDF soldier spoke to me.*
*And then I came back to my senses.*
*If it weren’t for these two, I wouldn’t have been able to stay sane.*
*We ran through the riverbed, one of them in front of me, the other behind.*
*I could hear the constant drone of the helicopters above me. Sometimes the searchlights got very close.*
*Each time they did, I hid in the piles of bodies until they passed.*
*I’d seen this many times before as I’d wandered through the world lines.*
*I’d seen death.*
*I’d seen the moments when people had died.*
*But at the same time, I’d never experienced what happened to a dead person after they were left out for a long time.*
*More than fear, more than sorrow, the thing that hit me first was the smell of death.*
*The rotting stench ate away at my body, not my soul.*
*My whole body was rejecting it.*
*It made me feel sick.*
*Thinking that way meant trampling on the dignity of the dead, but I couldn’t help it.*
*“The Valley of Hinnom.”*
*I remembered that phrase.*
*That was what that strange attacker had said that night, when they came after Dr. Leskinen, Maho, and me.*
Assailant: “It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the Valley of Hinnom.”
*That valley was the origin of the word Gehenna, meaning “hell.” It was said that flames burned there every night, scorching the heavens themselves.*
*Those who died merciless deaths with anger or misery in their hearts were flung into the flames, their souls becoming black smoke that rained hatred down on the land.*
*What I stared at now was Gehenna.*
*The two soldiers led me to a half-collapsed subway tunnel.*
*The lights were all off because there was no electricity, but there were three armored cars in camo colors, with their headlights on to illuminate the way.*
*They were four-wheel drive, off-road vehicles covered in thick chunks of armor, but I didn’t see any real weapons.*
SDF personnel: “You can take the subway route to escape to Saitama. I hear it’s still safe at Iruma Base. If you can get that far, you should be able to escape Kanto.”
Rintaro: “Escape... Kanto...?”
SDF personnel: “Ask them about it. For now, just hurry.”
*There were a lot of things I wanted to ask, but even as we spoke I heard what sounded like gunshots outside the tunnel. The men forced me into the back seat of one of the cars.*
SDF personnel: “Goodbye. I’ll be praying for your safety.”
Rintaro: “What? What about you guys?”
SDF personnel: “We have another mission to carry out. Farewell.”
*The two soldiers who had brought me here saluted, then turned around and left the station.*
*I felt like I was never going to see them again.*
*The door of the armored car slammed shut with a heavy thud.*
*The car’s crew were SDF soldiers, just a little older than me.*
*The diesel engine kicked to life, and the car raced down a tunnel that had originally been designed for trains.*
*Of course, it wasn’t a pleasant ride at all, but I didn’t have any choice.*
*There was no way I could tell them I wanted to go to Akihabara.*
*I had no way to alter the world line.*
*I had to survive in this hellish world.*
*And to survive, I needed to do what they said.*
*My wants didn’t matter at all. I wasn’t even allowed to express them.*
*I just did as they told me and ran.*
*It was all I could do.*
*But I had no idea that it would take an entire month.*
*The reason it took a month to get to Okinawa was that we were losing the war.*
*Supposedly, the plan had been to ferry me by plane to Okinawa once I’d arrived at Iruma Base.*
*But the constant bombing had slowed us down, so they gave up on the plane and decided I would escape to Kyushu by ground.*
*There was more than one attack by Soviet spies and assault teams. Some of the SDF soldiers protecting me died.*
*But when I got to Sasebo, I was able to get on a maritime SDF escort ship, and managed to escape to Okinawa.*
*Why were they doing all this for me?*
*No matter how many times I asked, no one would answer.*
*Okinawa in winter was covered in thick clouds.*
*Come to think of it, I hadn’t seen a real break in the clouds for a whole month.*
*I was thinking about that when I was loaded into a van with dark-tinted windows that had come to pick me up from the port.*
*Inside the car was not only the driver, but a middle-aged man sitting in the front passenger seat.*
*He was very short, perhaps only around 150 centimeters tall.*
*But he had the air of a military veteran, and even though he was fully dressed, I could tell he was extremely muscular.*
SDF personnel: “Rintaro Okabe, correct?”
SDF personnel: “I’m Shimoyama, with the Ministry of Defense’s Intelligence Security Command.”
Shimoyama: “We’re going to make a stop at the airport, and then head to the Okinawa Defense Bureau in Kadena. I’m sure you’re tired from your long journey, but I’ll have to ask you to hang in there a while longer.”
Rintaro: “...Right.”
*I’d heard that Tokyo had been destroyed.*
*The major functions of the Japanese government were now headquartered out of the Okinawa Defense Bureau, to allow for better cooperation with the American forces stationed nearby.*
*That’s what Shimoyama explained to me.*
*In other words, the place I was heading to was the core of Japan’s defenses.*
*Once I arrived, would I understand why I was so important that all those soldiers were willing to die to protect me?*
*The car stopped in front of Naha Airport for a while.*
*And then I saw a surprising pair get aboard.*
Yuki: “O-Okabe!”
Fubuki: “Wow, it’s really Okarin!”
Rintaro: “You’re... Yuki and Nakase!”
*I wasn’t expecting to see them there.*
*But they were the first people I knew who I’d met since coming to this world line.*
*That alone was almost enough to make me cry.*
*But still, I couldn’t just sit there and be happy.*
Rintaro: “What about Mayuri? Do you know where she is?”
Yuki: “She’s fine.”
*Yuki nodded, as if trying to make me feel better.*
Yuki: “She was just with us.”
Rintaro: “Just with you?”
Fubuki: “That’s right. Mayushii, and Rumiho, and Luka, and Kaede.”
Yuki: “We got to the airport this morning. We were all waiting because they said we could go to some place called the Defense Bureau, where we’d be safe.”
Yuki: “They just said they’d take Fubuki and me there first⋯”
Fubuki: “And then they had us get inside this car, where we found you.”
Rintaro: “Anyway, I’m glad everybody’s safe.”
*Since Daru and Suzuha weren’t mentioned, I was going to ask about them, but...*
Shimoyama: “Sorry, but can you talk about this later?”
*Shimoyama cut me off, and the car started moving.*
Shimoyama: “The plan is for your families to arrive at the Okinawa Defense Bureau eventually. We already have them under our protection.”
Fubuki: “R-Really?! I’m so glad⋯”
Shimoyama: “Your other friends are all in the car behind us. You haven’t been separated, so don’t worry.”
*I took a quick look, and saw another identical van a little behind us.*
*So Mayuri and the others were there?*
Yuki: “Then we’ll see them later, right?”
Shimoyama: “Of course.”
*Yuki let out a sigh of relief.*
Rintaro: “...”
*But then I started to wonder about something else.*
*Why were we split into different cars?*
*This van could hold at least another three people. If we squeezed tight it could easily hold everyone.*
*Or was there some reason they’d put me, Yuki, and Fubuki into the same car?*
*The car drove alongside the Okinawa monorail for a while, and then went south down a wide bypass.*
Rintaro: “It’s so dark...”
Yuki: “Huh? What was that?”
Rintaro: “Nothing, just... there are all these stores... but they’re all dark.”
*There were lots of franchise restaurants, big supermarkets, cafeterias for tourists, and rent-a-car places all jammed together along the side of the road.*
*But all of them were dead silent, and their lights were turned off.*
*Barely any of the street lights were turned on, and the only cars were Japanese and US military vehicles. I didn’t see anyone out walking.*
Shimoyama: “There’s a blackout in effect, as well as a curfew past 5:00 PM.”
Shimoyama: “Okinawa may be safe, but this is still wartime. Things can’t be like they were.”
Shimoyama: “I can’t wait for the war to end and everything to go back to normal.”
Rintaro: “...”
*Wartime, huh?*
Shimoyama: “Tell me, Okabe. The Okinawa you knew was a bright, fun place, even at night, wasn’t it?”
Rintaro: “Oh, I wouldn’t know. I’ve never been to Okinawa before.”
Shimoyama: “That’s a shame. Then I pray you get to come back for a good vacation sometime. This really is a nice island.”
*The car headed up from the bypass over a land bridge, and then to another road. We quickly came to a long tunnel.*
Shimoyama: “I actually wanted to ask the three of you some questions before we got to the Bureau. That’s why I have you riding with me.”
Fubuki: “Huh?”
Yuki: “...?”
Rintaro: “...”
*My guess was right.*
*That meant there was something he wanted to ask just the three of us.*
*But why us three?*
*I wasn’t particularly close to Yuki or Fubuki.*
*I’d only even started talking to them a few months ago–*
*And then I shook my head.*
*That was before the world line changed.*
*Maybe things were different in this world line.*
*I had no idea what my relationship was to anyone else in this world line.*
*Since the SDF had been treating me so well, I didn’t want to make Shimoyama suspicious.*
*I decided it would be best to leave most of the talking to Yuki and Fubuki.*
Shimoyama: “Yuki Amane.”
Yuki: “Y-Yes?”
*Shimoyama spoke to Yuki first.*
*Yuki went stiff when her name was called. I could feel it even sitting next to her.*
Shimoyama: “You don’t know where Itaru Hashida and his little sister are, do you?”
*Little sister...*
*That must be Suzuha.*
*That would mean that even in this world line Suzuha had come from the future, and gotten to know Yuki and the others while pretending to be Suzuha’s sister.*
*And the SDF evidently didn’t know where Daru and Suzuha were.*
Yuki: “No, I...”
*Yuki fell silent and glanced over to me, as if expecting help.*
*But I didn’t know where they were, either.*
*I didn’t even have any memories of this world line, so I had no way of answering.*
*But Yuki’s attitude bothered me.*
*It was as if she knew where they were and was deliberately hiding it, and that I was supposed to be hiding it, too.*
*I could figure that out, I’m sure Shimoyama could, too.*
*A strange tension filled the car.*
*Yuki was trying to hide it? From whom?*
Shimoyama: “Hmm? You’re sure you don’t know?”
*Shimoyama turned around from the front passenger seat and asked again.*
Yuki: “I’m sorry.”
*Yuki bowed her head in apology.*
Shimoyama: “But you were very close to him, weren’t you? You were his lover, and yet you heard nothing?”
Yuki: “You know that cell phones don’t work anymore, right?”
Shimoyama: “There are plenty of ways to get in touch with someone besides a cell phone.”
Yuki: “But I really don’t...”
Shimoyama: “Nothing from his sister, either?”
Yuki: “Nothing.”
Shimoyama: “By the way, I’m told that you were researching something with Hashida, Okabe?”
Rintaro: “Huh?”
*I wasn’t sure how to react when the conversation suddenly turned towards me.*
*Researching? Researching what?*
*Uh-oh. If I panic, I’ll make them suspicious.*
Shimoyama: “What were you researching?”
*I would just have to give him the most harmless answers I could.*
Rintaro: “It wasn’t really research... it was more like... inventions.”
Shimoyama: “Inventions?”
Rintaro: “Like whether you could attach a CCD camera to a bamboo copter to do aerial photography...”
Rintaro: “Or whether you could use the heat from a vacuum cleaner as a hair dryer...”
Shimoyama: “Oh? That’s interesting.”
Shimoyama: “Then you weren’t, say, making something unbelievable, and running away from us so that we wouldn’t find out what it was?”
Rintaro: “Running away?”
*Damn. I responded.*
*That was a mistake.*
*But did that mean that Daru and Suzuha were hiding from the SDF amidst all this chaos?*
*The SDF had risked their lives to protect me over the past month.*
*Shouldn’t I be asking them for help?*
*I got even more confused.*
Shimoyama: “If you don’t know, then that’s fine. We’ll talk about Hashida and his sister some other time.”
Rintaro: “...”
*Somebody, please tell me what the right answer is.*
*How am I supposed to respond here?*
Shimoyama: “Um... Katsumi Nakase? There was something else I wanted to ask you.”
Fubuki: “M-Me?”
*This time it was Fubuki’s turn to jump up in her seat.*
Shimoyama: “No, no. Don’t get so nervous. It’s nothing big.”
*Or so Shimoyama said, but Fubuki was clearly starting to get scared.*
*Her reaction was strange. It was too strong.*
*Maybe the Self-Defense Forces weren’t simply protecting us.*
*For one thing, there was no way normal civilians like us merited such important treatment.*
*But then what were they after?*
*No, I could guess.*
*The time machine.*
*This war started with Russia’s time machine experiments.*
*And of course, Nakabachi was involved. I’d learned from some of the soldiers that even in this world line he’d sought asylum in Russia.*
*And Suzuha was a time traveler from the year 2036.*
*If Suzuha was here in this era, that meant that it was Daru who made the time machine that brought her here.*
*If you had a time machine, you could change the outcome of this war.*
*It would make sense if that’s what the Japanese government thought, and if that was why they were trying to capture Daru, Suzuha, and their friends.*
*Once I realized that, the whole situation started to feel terrifying to me.*
*Was this car really headed toward the Okinawa Defense Bureau?*
*And if it was, were they really going to keep us safe there?*
Shimoyama: “About the physical you underwent last week...”
Fubuki: “W-Was there some problem?”
Shimoyama: “No. You’ve almost recovered from the wounds you sustained in Tokyo, and health-wise, you’re fine. But you’re under a lot of stress.”
Fubuki: “Oh...”
Shimoyama: “Well, it’s not surprising. You survived that terrible bombing. It’s no exaggeration to say that most civilians have PTSD now.”
Fubuki: “...”
Shimoyama: “But it seems that your symptoms are a little different than most people’s.”
Shimoyama: “You have very realistic dreams, for example.”
Shimoyama: “In particularly severe instances, they could almost be called waking dreams... I’m told at times you lose the ability to tell the difference between dreams and reality.”
Yuki: “Isn’t that just PTSD, though?”
*Fubuki was too scared to speak, so Yuki interrupted curtly.*
*It was rare to see Yuki act like this.*
*If nothing else, I’d never seen it before.*
*It was plain now.*
*Yuki didn’t trust Shimoyama. In fact, she considered him an enemy.*
Shimoyama: “No, it’s very strange...”
*Shimoyama paused a moment for effect, and rubbed his chin.*
Shimoyama: “There are others who say they have very similar dreams. And not just one or two.”
Fubuki: “What?”
Rintaro: “...”
Shimoyama: “Of course, the degree to which they suffer from this problem changes, but we’ve found more than ten in Japan alone.”
Shimoyama: “They exist in other countries, too. Well, we’ve only got information from the West...”
Rintaro: “That’s just a coincidence, isn’t it?”
*Fubuki was incredibly frightened.*
*So I spoke in her place.*
Shimoyama: “You’ve heard of Puchin, right?”
*Suddenly Shimoyama turned his gaze towards me, and asked me a question.*
Rintaro: “Puchin?”
Rintaro: “The Soviet... General Secretary, right?”
*I almost said the President of Russia, but managed to stop myself.*
*The Soviet Union still existed in this world line. Puchin’s title was General Secretary, not President. I’d heard that during my time at Iruma.*
Shimoyama: “Correct. But interestingly enough, Nakase referred to him as the President of Russia.”
*What?*
Fubuki: “I’m sorry. I wasn’t paying attention. And I’m not really what you’d call a good student.”
Shimoyama: “No, that’s not it. It’s one of the strange things about all the people who have these dreams. They all call him President Puchin.”
Fubuki: “...”
Shimoyama: “And they all call Golbachev and Leltsin presidents, too.”
Shimoyama: “That’s why the scientists have started calling it ‘President’s Disease.’ Not a terribly clever name, if you ask me.”
*N-No way...*
*Is he talking about... Reading Steiner?*
*There was a strong chance that people besides me had that power, even if not as acutely.*
*I’d never found out for sure, but what Faris had said in the alpha world line certainly suggested it.*
*So it was certainly possible that Shimoyama’s “waking dreams” were actually the effects of Reading Steiner.*
*If they were all aware of the world line shift a month ago, just like me...*
*If Fubuki had the same memories of the other world line that I had...*
*It would make perfect sense that she called Puchin a president.*
Yuki: “Golbachev? Leltsin?”
Shimoyama: “You don’t know them? Didn’t they teach that in world history?”
Yuki: “I only took science classes in high school...”
Shimoyama: “I thought everyone knew about them. Do kids today not know who they are? I find it hard to believe you’re all that ignorant.”
Shimoyama: “I’m sure you know about Golbachev and Leltsin, right, Okabe?”
Rintaro: “Y-Yeah, I suppose so.”
Shimoyama: “And perestroika, and the fall of the Berlin Wall.”
Rintaro: “Yeah, they were in the textbooks...”
*The second after the words were out of my mouth, an alarm went off in my mind.*
*–Something was wrong. There was something strange about what Shimoyama was saying.*
Rintaro: “...!”
*And then I realized.*
*The East and West were caught up in the middle of a World War. How could the Berlin Wall have fallen?*
*And could Golbachev really execute perestroika?*
*By the time I realized he’d tricked me, it was too late. My panic appeared on my face.*
Shimoyama: “Hmm?”
Shimoyama: “...You too, huh?”
Shimoyama: “And you were deliberately trying to hide it, weren’t you?”
Rintaro: “...”
Shimoyama: “So the information was right after all. You know something important.”
Shimoyama: “Listen, Okabe. I want you to tell me.”
*Shimoyama suddenly laughed. It was a bitter laugh, almost eerily so.*
Shimoyama: “Golbachev? Leltsin? Who are these people you all keep talking about?”
Shimoyama: “We don’t have any data on them, and neither do any of the American intelligence agencies. That data doesn’t exist.”
*Doesn’t exist?*
*I looked over at Yuki.*
Yuki: “...”
*From the look on her face I could tell that she really had no idea who they were.*
Shimoyama: “Perestroika? The Fall of the Berlin Wall? Did these things really happen?”
Shimoyama: “Tell me, please.”
*But I couldn’t answer.*
*I was thinking of something completely different.*
*I suddenly realized why the world line might have changed a month ago on Christmas Eve.*
*What if Russia used the time machine that day, in an experiment to change the past?*
*The goal of the experiment would’ve been to stop the collapse of the Soviet Union.*
*And if the result of them changing the past was this worldline...!*
*How foolish...!*
*A single change to the past and the butterfly effect makes the entire world so different.*
*Did they know how many people had died?*
Shimoyama: “Have you and your friends really experienced the history of a different world?”
Shimoyama: “I just can’t believe it. It’s just nonsense cooked up by some crazy scientists–”
*He was about to push me further when–*
*We heard the sound of an incoming call on a cell phone.*
Shimoyama: “Tch...”
*Shimoyama grunted and took his phone out of his pocket.*
Shimoyama: “This is Shimoyama.”
Shimoyama: “Yeah, we’re on our way to the Bureau.”
Shimoyama: “What? What do you mean?”
Shimoyama: “Damn it! That’s the problem with these idiots. What country do these politicians think they’re working for?”
*Shimoyama’s finger slammed down on the “end call” button so hard I thought the phone would break. There was a look of rage on his face.*
Shimoyama: “We’re changing our destination. Head to Kadena Base. Gate 2.”
*His words were filled with irritation as he spoke to the driver.*
*Changing destinations?*
*Who was he just talking to?*
*As I sat there confused, Shimoyama started to call someone else.*
Shimoyama: “This is Shimoyama. We’re changing our destination. We’ll meet at Gate 2 at Kadena Base.”
*That was all he said before he hung up.*
Yuki: “Um... what’s going on?”
Shimoyama: “The situation’s changed. Okabe is heading to a US military base.”
Shimoyama: “From there, he might get to take a fun trip on a US Air Force plane to America.”
Rintaro: “Wha-?!”
*America?!*
Shimoyama: “I’ll ask them to make sure you get first-class accommodations, but don’t get your hopes up. They don’t listen to us any more than you’d listen to a yapping pet dog.”
Rintaro: “Why America?!”
Shimoyama: “I don’t know if it’s the CIA or the NSC, but someone wants us to hand you over.”
Rintaro: “But why?!”
Shimoyama: “Ask them yourself.”
*And then he turned back towards the front and fell silent, refusing to answer any of my questions.*
*The car went down the road for a while, until we got off at an exit that read “South Okinawa.”*
*We stopped in front of the gate.*
*Several US soldiers had evidently been waiting for my arrival.*
Shimoyama: “Once we hand you over to the Americans, we’re not going to get any accurate information from them.”
Shimoyama: “So this is my last chance.”
*Shimoyama turned around from the front passenger seat and looked straight at me.*
*His eyes were desperate, and begging.*
Shimoyama: “Tell me. What are we supposed to do from now on?”
Rintaro: “...”
Shimoyama: “Please.”
*I remembered all the soldiers in Tokyo who’d fought so desperately to protect me.*
*Were they fighting to help someone else in Tokyo right now? Or were they already...?*
Rintaro: “I don’t know.”
Shimoyama: “Okabe...”
Rintaro: “I really don’t know.”
Rintaro: “Do you think I can do something about this war all by myself?”
Rintaro: “Knowing that Golbachev and Leltsin were presidents of Russia, or that they brought a dramatic end to the Cold War... that doesn’t actually help anything.”
Shimoyama: “...”
*I could hear the sound of another car getting closer.*
*Shimoyama sighed and opened the passenger side door.*
Shimoyama: “Get out.”
*I exited the car as I was told.*
Mayuri: “Okarin!”
Rintaro: “...!”
*Mayuri got out of the van behind us and ran over to me.*
Rintaro: “Mayuri...!”
Mayuri: “Okarin!”
*My childhood friend flung herself into my arms, and I held her tight.*
Mayuri: “I finally... get to see you.”
Rintaro: “I’m so glad you’re safe...”
*I could feel her warmth.*
*Mayuri was here.*
*I’d never gone almost a whole month without seeing her before.*
*And this was wartime. I couldn’t easily contact her like I could in the old world line.*
*So I’d been so worried about whether or not Mayuri was okay.*
*It was no exaggeration to say that I’d survived this far just to make sure.*
*I’d erased the entire alpha world line to save her.*
*No matter what happened, I wanted her to be safe.*
Mayuri: “Okarin... you’re hurting me!”
Rintaro: “Oh, sorry.”
*I’d held her too closely.*
*I took a step back.*
Mayuri: “Mayushii believed, you know.”
Mayuri: “Mayushii believed she’d get to see Okarin again.”
Rintaro: “Yeah...”
Faris: “Hooray! You’re safe, nya!”
Luka: “Okabe!”
